description: C++ Inheritance, Types of Inheritance, Base and Derived Classes, Access and Constructor Order

questions.questionText: What is inheritance in C++?
questions.optionA: A method of converting data types
questions.optionB: A mechanism by which a class acquires properties and behavior of another class
questions.explanation: Inheritance allows a derived class to acquire accessible members and behavior from a base class.

questions.questionText: What is the class from which another class inherits called?
questions.explanation: The class being inherited from is called the base class or parent class.

questions.questionText: What is the class that inherits from another class called?
questions.explanation: The class that inherits from a base class is called the derived class.

questions.questionText: Which symbol is used to specify inheritance between classes?
questions.explanation: A colon is used in the class declaration to specify the base class.

questions.questionText: Which declaration correctly represents public inheritance?
questions.explanation: C++ uses the syntax class B : public A to derive B publicly from A.

questions.questionText: Which type of inheritance involves one derived class inheriting from one base class?
questions.explanation: Single inheritance has one base class and one derived class.

questions.questionText: Which type of inheritance involves a derived class inheriting from more than one base class?
questions.explanation: Multiple inheritance occurs when one derived class has more than one base class.

questions.questionText: Which type of inheritance forms a chain such as A -> B -> C?
questions.explanation: In multilevel inheritance, a class is derived from another derived class, forming a chain.

questions.questionText: Which type of inheritance has multiple derived classes inheriting from the same base class?
questions.explanation: Hierarchical inheritance occurs when multiple derived classes inherit from one base class.

questions.questionText: What is hybrid inheritance?
questions.optionD: A combination of two or more types of inheritance
questions.explanation: Hybrid inheritance combines two or more forms of inheritance.

questions.questionText: Which access specifier allows a derived class to directly access inherited members while preventing general outside access?
questions.explanation: Protected members are accessible inside the class and its derived classes.

questions.questionText: Are private members of a base class directly accessible in a derived class?
questions.explanation: Private base-class members cannot be directly accessed by derived classes.

questions.questionText: What happens to public members of a base class under public inheritance?
questions.explanation: With public inheritance, public base members remain public in the derived class.

questions.questionText: What happens to protected members of a base class under public inheritance?
questions.explanation: Protected members remain protected under public inheritance.

questions.questionText: What is the default inheritance mode for a C++ class?
questions.explanation: For a class, inheritance is private by default if no access specifier is specified.

questions.questionText: What is the default inheritance mode for a C++ struct?
questions.explanation: For a struct, inheritance is public by default.

questions.questionText: In what order are constructors called when creating an object of a derived class?
questions.optionA: Base class first, then derived class
questions.optionC: Derived class first, then base class
questions.explanation: The base-class constructor executes before the derived-class constructor.

questions.questionText: In what order are destructors called when a derived object is destroyed?
questions.explanation: Destruction occurs in reverse order: the derived destructor runs before the base destructor.

questions.questionText: What is the output? class A { public: A() { cout << "A"; } }; class B : public A { public: B() { cout << "B"; } }; int main() { B obj; }
questions.explanation: The base constructor A executes first, followed by the derived constructor B.

questions.questionText: What is the output? class A { public: ~A() { cout << "A"; } }; class B : public A { public: ~B() { cout << "B"; } }; int main() { B obj; }
questions.explanation: The derived destructor executes first, followed by the base destructor.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to explicitly call a base-class constructor from a derived-class constructor's initializer list?
questions.explanation: The base class constructor is called by writing the base class name in the derived constructor's initializer list.

questions.questionText: Which inheritance type is represented by class C : public A, public B?
questions.explanation: Class C inherits from two base classes, A and B, so this is multiple inheritance.

questions.questionText: Which inheritance type is represented by A -> B -> C?
questions.explanation: A chain of inheritance such as A -> B -> C represents multilevel inheritance.

questions.questionText: If class B publicly inherits class A, which member of A cannot be directly accessed by B?
questions.explanation: Private members of the base class are not directly accessible in the derived class.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of inheritance in OOP?
questions.optionC: Code reuse and establishing an is-a relationship
questions.explanation: Inheritance promotes code reuse and models an is-a relationship between classes.
